effect: The supporting cells built fibres around themselves, completing the chapter. The result contrasts proteins kept inside muscle cells with material released around supporting cells.
reaction: The comparison helped the two paths make sense, though their steps felt similar.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the pulling proteins was most worthwhile: the picture showed how overlapping fibres can slide to shorten a cell, connecting the protein to the cell’s job.

leastWorthwhile.text: The supporting-cell path repeated much of the muscle path, so choosing its matching messenger and then amino acids felt predictable, even though the comparison was useful.

surprise.text: I was surprised that cells with the same DNA and building blocks could end up with proteins in different places: inside muscle cells or around supporting cells.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary; the pictures and earlier protein-building example gave each pairing a purpose. The details of how the messengers cause different genes to become active were not explained.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, mainly to see how the separate muscle cells are assembled into larger fibres and how their pulling proteins help movement.
